title: The Ordinary’s $9 Caffeine Serum Revives My Tired Skin Better Than Makeup
text:
The Ordinary’s $9 Caffeine Serum Revives My Tired Skin Better Than Makeup

If you’re buying, mine’s a flat white with an extra shot and a dash of hazelnut syrup. And while I prefer to get my caffeine fix in coffee form, it seems I might be missing a trick when it comes to skincare.

This month, The Ordinary lifted the lid on its new Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, which it calls an “energizing face serum to instantly refresh tired-looking skin.” As a longtime fan of all things The Ordinary, and who recently went through a stressful period that led to dullness, breakouts, and hyperpigmentation, it went straight into my bathroom cabinet.

Here’s everything you need to know about the new product and why it’s already racking up hundreds of five-star reviews.

The Ordinary Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, $9

What is The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, and what are the benefits?

According to The Ordinary, the latest addition to its burgeoning serum family firms, energizes, tones, and tightens skin. These are certainly bold claims, but the brand believes it can back them up with a handful of effective ingredients.

First up, caffeine. Consultant dermatologist Dr. Derrick Phillips tells me that while we’re often advised to limit the amount of caffeine we consume, applying it to the skin is a different story. “Caffeine is used in skincare for its antioxidant properties,” says Dr. Phillips, which helps protect skin against dulling environmental aggressors like pollution and UV.

There’s more. “Its ability to temporarily constrict blood vessels can help to reduce the appearance of puffiness, which is why it is commonly included in under-eye creams and serums,” adds Dr. Phillips. He explains that when applied topically, caffeine acts locally rather than having the whole-body stimulating effects associated with drinking coffee. That said, the results are generally temporary, explains Dr. Phillips: “It will all depend on the concentration of caffeine and the overall formulation of the product,” he says, “but it can be a useful ingredient for making the eye area look less puffy and more refreshed.”

Then there’s escin, not to be mistaken for ectoin, the moisturizing ingredient. I consider myself something of an ingredient know-it-all, but even I hadn’t heard of it before. Dr. Phillips says that escin, also known as aescin, is a mixture of naturally occurring compounds called triterpenoid saponins. “These are derived from horse chestnut seeds,” says Dr. Phillips, adding, “Escin has anti-inflammatory and anti-swelling properties, which is why it is sometimes included in skincare designed to soothe the skin and reduce the appearance of puffiness.” Escin could also provide similar antioxidant benefits to caffeine, but Dr. Phillips says that the research on its skin rewards is currently lacking.

Besides these two, there’s also dry skin-quenching glycerin — an ingredient I look out for in all my serums and moisturizers. Not only is it non-comedogenic, so less likely to clog pores and cause breakouts, but it’s also considered a humectant, so it draws much-needed moisture into the skin, making it smooth and plump.

What makes The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum special?

The multiple five-star reviews for The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum speak for themselves. One user says they wouldn’t be without the serum, while another praises its ability to make their skin appear more awake and energized. One simply refers to it as “age-reverse.”

Since incorporating it into my skincare routine over the last three weeks, I’ve been wearing much less foundation and concealer because I’m convinced my skin looks brighter, radiant, and more even in tone. Applying a full pump of CC cream has felt like a little too much for me, which I think is a testament to the 3% caffeine. Thanks to the high concentration of glycerin, my skin feels a lot more moisturized, too, and on some days, when it’s too hot for a full skincare routine, I just apply a generous amount of the serum.

I haven’t noticed any change in my facial structure, but serums in general can only do so much, and it seems Dr. Phillips agrees: “A topical serum may temporarily reduce puffiness and improve hydration, which can make the skin appear fresher, smoother and slightly more defined, but the effects of a serum are limited to the skin,” he tells me. It’s not all about your collagen, either, as Dr. Phillips explains: “Facial shape and structure are also influenced by the underlying muscles, ligaments, fat compartments, and facial skeleton, which a topical product cannot alter.”

That said, at a recent beauty event, an editor peer took one look at me and asked if I’d had work done. I hadn’t — just the serum — but when I asked what they were thinking, they said my skin looked smoother and glowing, sort of like a Botox effect. Interestingly, Dr. Phillips says that any immediate lifting or contouring effects like these from serums are likely temporary, thanks to a boost in the skin’s hydration levels or reduced puffiness. Still, I’m impressed.

What to know about The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum

• Contains 3% caffeine and 1% escin to boost hydration, radiance, and firmness, while bacillus ferment keeps skin strong and supple.

• Can help reduce morning puffiness when massaged into the skin for one to three minutes.

• Suitable for all skin types and can be used in the morning and evening.

How do you use The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, and is it worth it?

I find that hydrating, milky serums like this work best when applied after cleansing (to dry skin) and before moisturizer or sunscreen. In the morning, I wash my face with a gentle cleanser (I like Dermalogica Magnetic[+] Afterglow Cleanser) and pat a pipette-full of the serum onto my skin. Once it’s absorbed, I wait a couple of minutes before applying my sunscreen — Thankyou Farmer Sun Project Light Sun Essence SPF 50+. Because this feels so replenishing, I tend to skip moisturizer altogether. In the evening, I double cleanse, apply the serum, and follow with Hada Labo Tokyo Plumping Gel Cream. A few nights a week, I swap the serum for retinal to exfoliate and keep my hormonal skin in check.

If you’re after an instant glow boost without the need for makeup, you won’t be disappointed by this serum. Who knows, people might even think you’ve had a tweakment here or there…

Where can you get The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum?

The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum retails for $9 and is available at theordinary.com, ulta.com, and nordstrom.com.

title: Your Horoscope This Week: August 2 To 8
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: August 2 To 8

Cosmic beings, this first full week of August feels like a much-needed exhale after making it through Mercury retrograde in July and the beginning of Saturn retrograde. We do have one more retrograde starting on August 3rd, with Chiron retrograding in Taurus, but this is a much quieter, more behind-the-scenes energy that won’t be felt as potently as Mercury or Saturn. It’s more of a gentle reminder to tend to the body, tend to the earth, return to simple pleasures, and give more presence and love to the parts of us that still need healing.

We’re being invited to begin August with greater sensitivity toward our wounds without becoming consumed by them, and to remember that healing can also look practical: eating well, resting, moving our bodies, spending time outside, decluttering, or returning to the small rituals that help us feel more grounded, empowered, and whole.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra, one of the signs it feels most at home in, and the energy becomes noticeably sweeter. For the past four weeks, Venus in Virgo had us looking at love, beauty, friendships, and even ourselves through a more critical, practical, or analytical lens, which may not have felt especially romantic or carefree.

Now, over the next four weeks, the collective becomes more pleasure-oriented, beauty-oriented, and love-oriented. It becomes easier to open our hearts to both platonic and romantic connection, create simply because it feels good, flirt, play, dress up, and indulge in the beauty around us. This softer energy arrives right on time as we enter eclipse month, giving us space to enjoy ourselves before the cosmos starts shaking things up again.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, this week asks you to soften your grip a little and stop treating every insecurity like an emergency meeting. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your money, security, and self-worth sector on August 3rd, bringing your relationship with finances, your body, and the way you view yourself up for review. You may become more aware of where fear has been shaping your spending, saving, or confidence, but with Saturn already retrograde in your sign, you don’t need to investigate every feeling until it files a full report. A little healthy detachment will help you learn from what comes up without becoming consumed by it.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and brings one of the sweetest, most refreshing shifts you’ve experienced in the past month. With the planet of love moving through your partnership sector, you’re more open to aﬀection, romance, and actually enjoying the people in front of you. Existing relationships can feel more fulfilling, while single and dating Aries may notice more options, more mutual interest, and less pressure to figure out the entire future by date two.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, this week is personal, and there’s no hiding behind being “fine” when your body, confidence, or emotions are clearly asking for more care. Chiron begins its retrograde in your sign on August 3rd, bringing your identity, self-image, and the way you move through the world up for review. You may feel more sensitive about your appearance, more aware of how others receive you, or unexpectedly triggered by an old version of yourself you thought you had outgrown. Move through it by staying present instead of turning every discomfort into a full identity crisis. Dress in a way that makes you feel good, move your body, spend time outside, and let yourself evolve without needing to explain the transformation while it’s still happening.

Then, on August 6th, your ruler Venus enters Libra, another sign it rules, and settles into your health, wellness, and routine sector. This is your reminder that self-care works best when it actually feels good. Get the facial, book the haircut, clean your sheets, take the long shower, go to bed earlier, and please stop doom-scrolling like the answers to your life are hiding in someone else’s comment section. The more lovingly you tend to yourself, the better you feel, the brighter your aura becomes, and the more naturally other people are drawn to you.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, this week reminds you that you can talk your way around a feeling for only so long before it circles back with receipts. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your spirituality and subconscious sector on August 3rd, bringing buried emotions, old fears, and unprocessed thoughts closer to the surface. Give yourself enough alone time to hear what’s actually going on beneath the mental noise. Journaling, meditation, long walks, less stimulation, and simply sitting with yourself can help you process what you feel before it spills out impulsively or overwhelms you later.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters fellow Air sign Libra and lights up your fate, romance, creativity, and dating sector. This is easily one of the most fun and flirtatious transits you’ve experienced in a while, so let yourself enjoy it without turning every interaction into a five-year plan. Take yourself out, be open to being courted, flirt back, create something beautiful, and let pleasure lead. If you’re already in a relationship, date your partner like you’re meeting them again for the first time and remember what made you curious about each other in the first place.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, this week helps you get clearer about who deserves access to your energy. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your friendship, community, and social network sector on August 3rd, bringing old wounds around belonging, rejection, comparison, or feeling left out back into focus. You may notice where you’ve been overextending yourself to stay connected, shrinking to fit into certain groups, or measuring your progress against what everyone else is posting. Spend more time with the people who make you feel safe enough to be yourself, and step back from spaces that keep reopening the same insecurity.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and moves into your home, family, and roots sector, making your private life feel warmer and more inviting. This is a beautiful time to redecorate, host people you love, repair a family connection, or create more peace in your living space. Buy the flowers, revamp your space, cook something comforting, and make your home feel like somewhere your nervous system can actually relax.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, this week puts your relationship with success under a microscope, especially the parts no one sees behind the applause. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your career, reputation, and public image sector on August 3rd, bringing old insecurities around achievement, recognition, leadership, or being taken seriously back into focus. You may question whether you’re doing enough, compare your timeline to someone else’s, or feel more sensitive to feedback from bosses, clients, or the public. Pay attention to where your ambition is being fueled by purpose versus the need to prove yourself. You can update your goals, strengthen your professional boundaries, and let your work speak without tying your entire identity to how quickly others validate it.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and brings more ease, charm, and connection to your communication sector. Your words land more smoothly, conversations feel more playful, and people are more receptive to your ideas, humor, and perspective.

This is a strong transit for writing, pitching, content creation, interviews, short trips, and reconnecting with siblings or people in your local community. Let yourself be social, send the message, share the thought, and say yes to plans that get you out of the house. You may also notice that flirting comes naturally now, especially through witty banter, DMs, or a conversation that starts casually and becomes much more interesting than expected.

Virgo Sun & Rising:

Virgo, this week puts your beliefs, long-term plans, and sense of direction up for review. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your expansion sector on August 3rd, bringing up old insecurities around travel, education, teaching, entrepreneurship, or whether you’re truly qualified to pursue the life you want. You may question a path you once felt certain about, revisit a dream you postponed, or realize that someone else’s definition of success has been shaping your choices more than your own. Give yourself permission to learn as you go. You don’t need every credential, answer, or detail mapped out before taking the next step.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and moves into your money, self-worth, and values sector, making it easier to attract support and enjoy what you’ve worked for. This can bring opportunities to increase your income, raise your rates, improve your budget, or spend on something that genuinely adds beauty and ease to your life. You may also feel more confident in your appearance and less interested in picking yourself apart. Let pleasure be part of your financial plan too, Virgo. You’re allowed to save responsibly and still buy the good coffee, upgrade your space, or wear something that makes you feel expensive.

Libra Sun & Rising:

Libra, this week brings your relationship with trust, intimacy, and shared resources into sharper focus. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your transformation sector on August 3rd, bringing up old wounds around vulnerability, debt, dependence, betrayal, or feeling like you have to manage everything alone. You may notice where you’ve been over-giving, avoiding a financial conversation, or staying emotionally guarded because closeness once came with consequences. Use the next few months to clean up what feels complicated, whether that means setting clearer boundaries, reviewing shared expenses, asking for support, or being more honest about what you need before resentment starts doing the talking.

Then, on August 6th, your ruler Venus enters your sign, and you begin feeling more like yourself again. Your confidence, magnetism, style, and social ease all get a boost, making this an ideal time to refresh your look, update your photos, attend more events, flirt, create, and let people come toward you. You may notice that others are more receptive to your energy and more willing to offer compliments, invitations, or romantic attention. Use the next four weeks to enjoy being seen without overthinking how you’re being perceived. The more comfortable you feel in your own skin, the more naturally your charm does the rest.

Scorpio Sun & Rising:

Scorpio, this week brings your closest relationships into focus, especially the ones that activate old wounds around trust, rejection, or feeling misunderstood. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your partnership sector on August 3rd, encouraging you to notice the patterns that repeat in love, friendship, and one-on-one collaborations. You may become more aware of where you expect disappointment, test people before they’ve done anything wrong, or stay in dynamics that keep confirming an old insecurity. Use this retrograde to communicate more directly, strengthen your boundaries, and choose relationships where vulnerability feels mutual rather than like a risk only you are taking.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and moves into your spirituality, healing, and solitude sector. Your desire for privacy may increase, but this can be a deeply restorative and romantic transit when you stop forcing yourself to stay socially available. Spend time creating, resting, journaling, listening to music, or enjoying beauty without needing to share the moment online. A private crush, hidden attraction, or past love could also resurface, so make sure nostalgia is not making the decision for you. The more time you give yourself to recharge, the clearer you’ll become about what kind of love and connection actually feels peaceful.

Sagittarius Sun & Rising:

Sagittarius, this week shows you exactly where your daily habits are supporting you and where they’ve been running on fumes. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your health, work, and routine sector on August 3rd, bringing old insecurities around productivity, discipline, your body, or feeling useful back into focus. You may become more aware of how stress shows up physically, where your schedule has become unsustainable, or how often you ignore your own needs until your body starts filing formal complaints. Use this retrograde to simplify your routine, follow through on appointments, adjust your workload, and build habits that help you feel stronger instead of constantly behind.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and lights up your friendship, community, and social network sector. The next four weeks are made for reconnecting, collaborating, attending events, meeting new people, and spending more time with friends who bring out your most playful and inspired side. A friendship could become romantic, a mutual connection could introduce you to someone interesting, or an online opportunity may open through your network. Let people support you, Sag. Your social life can become a source of joy and momentum now, especially when you stop assuming every adventure has to begin with you organizing the group chat.

Capricorn Sun & Rising:

Capricorn, this week brings your relationship with joy, creativity, romance, and self-expression up for review. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your fate, dating, and
inner child sector on August 3rd, bringing up old insecurities around being chosen, being seen, or feeling talented enough to share what you create. You may notice where fear of rejection has made you hold back, where you’ve treated pleasure like a reward, or where you’ve become so focused on being responsible that play keeps getting pushed to the bottom of the list. Make room for the hobby, the date, the idea, or the version of yourself that doesn’t need to turn everything into a five-year plan.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and moves into your career, reputation, and public image sector, making you more visible, persuasive, and well-received professionally. This is a strong transit for interviews, pitches, launches, leadership opportunities, and any moment when charm matters just as much as competence. People are more likely to notice your style, your ideas, and the way you carry yourself, so let your presentation match the level you’re stepping into. Update the bio, schedule the meeting, and stop acting surprised when the room responds well to you.

Aquarius Sun & Rising:

Aquarius, this week brings your relationship with home, family, and emotional security up for review. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your roots sector on August 3rd, which can stir old wounds connected to childhood, belonging, family expectations, or never quite feeling settled. You may become more aware of how much your living environment affects your nervous system, or where you’ve been carrying family dynamics that were never yours to fix. Use this retrograde to create more safety in the present through stronger boundaries, a calmer home, honest conversations, or simply giving yourself permission to build a life that feels different from the one you inherited.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters fellow Air sign Libra and moves into your expansion, travel, education, and publishing sector. This can bring more ease around trips, creative opportunities, teaching, learning, and connecting with people who widen your perspective. You may feel drawn to book a getaway, apply for a program, share your work with a larger audience, or say yes to something that feels adventurous and a little glamorous. Romance can also show up through travel, school, or someone from a different background, so keep your mind open and your passport somewhere you can actually find it.

Pisces Sun & Rising:

Pisces, this week puts your thoughts, communication style, and mental habits under review. Chiron in Taurus begins its retrograde in your communication and learning sector on August 3rd, bringing up old insecurities around speaking up, being misunderstood, feeling intelligent enough, or worrying that your ideas won’t be taken seriously. You may revisit a conversation, writing project, class, or message you’ve been avoiding, or notice how quickly your mind turns one awkward moment into a full documentary. Slow down before reacting, write things out, ask for clarification, and give yourself space to say what you actually mean.

Then, on August 6th, Venus enters Libra and moves into your intimacy, transformation, and shared-resources sector. This can bring more ease to conversations about trust, sex, money, debt, support, and what you’re building with someone else. You may feel more open to deepening a relationship, receiving help, renegotiating a financial arrangement, or letting someone see a more vulnerable side of you. Attraction becomes more intense too, so enjoy the chemistry, but keep your standards awake. The right connection should feel magnetic without leaving you confused about where you stand.

title: The Real Difference Between A $29 Cashmere Sweater And A $295 One
text:
The Real Difference Between A $29 Cashmere Sweater And A $295 One

There is a specific kind of disappointment reserved for cheap cashmere. You buy an “air-conditioned mall” knit thinking you’ve outsmarted the luxury market. It feels deceptively soft on the hanger, but the moment you wear it out into the world, the illusion shatters. After one afternoon, the silhouette sags, the cuffs stretch out, and an aggressive, fuzzy haze of pilling forms along the underarms almost immediately. By wear number three, it’s just embarrassing.

Which begs an obvious shopping question: What actually justifies the leap from a high-street knit to a $295-plus investment piece? Is it just brand prestige, or is there tangible, physical proof woven into the threads?

To find out, I traveled to Northern Italy with luxury knitwear house Falconeri, tracing the journey of a single garment from raw material to finished product. Visiting their yarn mills in Biella and their facility and HQ in Avio, I watched every stage of production unfold. What I discovered is that true cashmere quality isn’t necessarily built in a flash of genius. It’s layered, step by painstaking step, kinda like a good lasagna. Here is what separates run-of-the-mill knits from pieces built to last for years (and how to make sure your investment stays pristine for years to come).

DashDividers_1_500x100

Long Versus Short Fibers

The quality gap begins long before a single thread is spun into yarn. On the factory floor in Biella, the first thing that hit me was the sheer scale of the raw material: massive pallets of fluffy raw Mongolian goat hair arriving straight from the pastures. Holding that raw undercoat in its bulk form before its undergone any industrial processing is like touching wearable cotton candy, without the stickiness. It’s extraordinarily soft, super light, and extremely delicate.

Even if the source is the same, here’s where the budget brands cut costs: They rely on short, thick, leftover fibers (often the sweepings or coarse outer hairs) to whip together their sweaters. Because short fibers don’t have enough length to anchor securely into a yarn, their raw ends stick out. The moment your arms rub against your sides, those loose ends roll into immediate, stubborn pills.

High-tier houses source long, ultrathin fibers from the goat’s undercoat. Long-staple fibers interlock tightly when twisted, creating a smooth, strong yarn that resists surface friction and retains its softness without disintegrating.

DashDividers_1_500x100

The Factories

Seeing the raw fiber was impressive, but the technical yarn-spinning process was where the engineering clicked for me. Falconeri operates an entire factory dedicated exclusively to turning raw fleece into refined yarn. Inside, every batch of fiber is dyed, conditioned with natural oils, rested for a week to balance moisture, and precisely carded or combed. Optical sensors continuously scan the moving threads, automatically cutting out even micro-imperfections before the strands are twisted together. From there, the yarn travels to a second dedicated facility in Avio, where it is transformed into the actual garments.

This isn’t mass assembly. It is high-precision craftsmanship. I watched skilled seamstresses painstakingly hand-link individual threads to state-of-the-art Japanese knitting machines, ensuring seams lie completely flat and never pull or distort over time. When you watch a single garment pass through dozens of hands, sensors, and quality checks, the cost-per-wear makes total sense.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Year-Round Styling

Because high-quality cashmere is naturally thermoregulating, treating it solely as a “winter sweater” is a missed opportunity. Fine-gauge knits belong in your wardrobe rotation 365, 24/7. I put my ultrafine sweater to the test in the scorching summer of Milan, wearing it with my go-to capris and kitten heels. Tying it around your neck is always a smart option, too. It especially comes in handy when the air conditioner is blasting indoors. For cool fall mornings, I plan on letting a thin white T-shirt peek from underneath the V-neckline and wearing it with everything, from jeans to pencil skirts.

DashDividers_1_500x100

The Cashmere Care

The most shocking insight from my conversations with the craftsmen in Milan came down to laundry care. Like most people, I had spent years assuming cashmere was strictly a “dry clean only” situation (probably because of the nightmare experiences I’ve had in the past with synthetic hybrids). The artisans laughed at that idea because dry cleaning uses harsh chemicals that strip the fiber’s natral oils over time. Their actual directive? Cashmere loves water. You can safely wash your knits in a standard washing machine provided you use a low-tumble, delicate cycle with cold water and gentle detergent. Low friction is the goal.

Next you’ll want to get ahead of pilling and comb your sweater before it starts. The craftsman showed me how running a fine cashmere comb lightly over friction points catches stray strands before they form those dense pills.

Lastly, remember that gravity is the enemy. Heavy hangers stretch the shoulder seams and ruin the necklines on structured knits. So never hang them. Instead, lay them flat to dry or store them folded.

DashDividers_1_500x100

The Investment Pieces

If you’re ready to build a knitwear collection that actually lasts, skip the fast-fashion rack and focus on versatile, long-fiber staples. You aren’t just paying for a label when you upgrade your knitwear. You are paying for a piece of sartorial joy that holds its shape, honors Italian craftsmanship, and gets softer every time it touches water. Skip the $29 sweaters that end up in the donation bin by November, and invest in a knit that will earn its keep for years and years to come.

title: Here’s Everything We Know About Children Of Blood and Bone — & Its Controversy
text:
Here’s Everything We Know About Children Of Blood and Bone — & Its Controversy

The Children of Blood and Bone controversy may not be coming to an end anytime soon. After the trailer for the Paramount Pictures film adaptation of the bestselling novel dropped on Tuesday, author Tomi Adeyemi doubled down on her decision to distance herself from the project. She shared in a TikTok video that working on the film was “the worst thing I have ever had to live through” that resulted in her “hyperventilating” to the point where she had to leave the set.

“There are many witnesses, so it’s not really a secret,” the Nigerian-American author said in the video. “I came back to America and suffered such severe somatic pain and so many panic attacks. I knew it was so bad that I would never ever be able to watch this film, and I made peace with that.”

@tomi.adeyemi #childrenofbloodandbone ♬ original sound – tomi adeyemi

Fans are wondering what actually happened for Adeyemi to entirely cut ties. Calling this adaptation highly anticipated would be an understatement. The film, shot in IMAX, projected to be a big screen blockbuster that could rival the impact of The Hunger Games and has been compared to the expansive world of Harry Potter. With a star-studded cast, and direction by Gina Prince-Bythewood, Children of Blood and Bone could open new doors in the fantasy film genre when it hits theaters January 15, 2027. 

Though Adeyemi nor the filmmakers have given much detail about what happened behind the scenes, some fans are wondering what the controversy means for the project. Though Adeyemi has announced herself that she will not be seeing the adaptation of her novel, she has not sent a call-to-action for her fans to also abstain from the film. In fact, in response to a comment on a since-deleted TikTok video, the 32-year old said “I do not mind anyone going to watch the film.” She continued, “I wrote this for us. I fought for us. I’m just laying down my sword and officially separating my name because I can’t keep being hurt and attacked behind the scenes.”

Audiences have mixed feelings about the film. Some have expressed that they, too, will be sitting this one out to support Adeyemi, while others feel like the roles Amandla Stenberg and other cast members hold should’ve been for Nigerian actors. Still, some fans’ support for the film hasn’t wavered, especially considering the unfair standards Black filmmakers face when studios look at box office numbers.

This is an unfortunate controversy. Children of Blood and Bone has had a generational impact as a YA novel that has broken barriers for how big fantasy that centers Black characters can be. And though it is not the first text based in Africa that uses magic, spirituality and cultural tradition to weave together a stunningly resonant story, it is the first of its kind to get the massive budgeting and Hollywood hype typically reserved for films with white-dominant casting. It’s expected to become one of the biggest fantasy features next year. Many worry that if this film doesn’t meet the mark at the box office, it may be a long time before another Black writer or director — let alone a Black woman — gets to showcase a fantastical world at this level. 

We may not know the root cause of the controversy but here’s a timeline of how we got here.

March 6, 2018: Tomi Adeyemi publishes Children of Blood and Bone

At 24, Tomi Adeyemi released Children of Blood and Bone, the first of three books in her groundbreaking Legacy of Orïsha series. The YA novel is set in a fictional African nation where protagonist Zélie Adebola sets out to bring magic back to the people of her kingdom who have been stripped of their power by an oppressive regime. Published by Henry Holt Books for Young Readers, Adeyemi received a historic book deal that included preemptive filmmaking rights which sold to Fox 2000 Pictures. Children of Blood and Bone debuted at No. 1 on New York Times’ Bestsellers List and spent over 120 weeks in the rankings. The Nigerian-American author also has earned several literary awards and was named on the Time 100 list in 2019 and 2020. 

January 2022: Adeyemi lands a seven-figure deal with Paramount Pictures 

The film was initially developed under George Lucas’ Lucasfilm with This Is Us writer Kay Oyegun penning the script and Rick Famuyiwa directing. After Disney’s acquisition of 20th Century Fox, Lucasfilm let the rights on the film lapse. A major bidding war ensued between studios, including Universal, Amazon and Netflix. Paramount Pictures came out victorious, obtaining the rights to the Children of Blood and Bone trilogy, which also includes Children of Virtue and Vengeance (December 2019) and Children of Anguish and Anarchy (June 2024). When first announced, Deadline reported that her deal included a seven-figure screenwriting guarantee, creative approvals for the author as executive producer and a guaranteed theatrical release.

“Paramount’s passion and enthusiasm to bring this story to life has been incredible,” Adeyemi told the trade outlet at the time. “We are all so excited for this new chapter and are already hard at work.”

December 14, 2023: Gina Prince-Bythewood announced as director

Prince-Bythewood entered the project as its new director. She also co-wrote the script with Adeyemi with her husband, Reggie Rock Bythewood, serving as an executive producer. The Love & Basketball director said that she was approached to take the helm of Children of Blood and Bone three times over the course of seven years, noting that the timing wasn’t right the first two times. When she was approached the third time, she had The Woman King and The Old Guard under her belt. She noted that those films gave her the technical and emotional readiness to tell the story.

“I couldn’t say no,” she told the Los Angeles Times. “It was something even bigger in a space that we hadn’t got to see ourselves in, which is fantasy and big, epic fantasy.”

Since being named director, both Prince-Bythewood and Adeyemi have discussed their alignment on record. In June 2024, Adeyemi sang the director’s praises in an interview with Elle. “What Gina does so well is tell these deep, complex stories of women who look like us front and center, with incredible action set pieces, incredible cinematography,” she said. “It feels divine. It feels bigger than [just] making this project. We’re really in sync.” 

This month, Prince-Bythewood told Essence that co-signing on the film with Adeyemi “was everything.” She said they were aligned through scripting, artwork and more. “And that’s inspiring as a director because again, we’re here because of something that came from her and we want to honor that,” the director said.

January 22, 2025: The principal cast draws initial criticism

Thuso Mbedu, Damson Idris and Amandla Stenberg lead this ensemble cast, which also includes Viola Davis, Regina King, Idris Elba, Cynthia Erivo, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Zackary Momoh, Tosin Cole and Lashana Lynch. A predominantly Black cast with major star power wasn’t enough to quell audiences’ concerns over certain casting choices, however. Readers called out colorism after Stenberg was announced as one of the main protagonists, who is described as having “dark copper skin” and contends with colorism and fatphobia in the book. Folks also took issue with a lack of Nigerian representation, pointing to the novel’s Yoruba roots.

Stenberg, who also received similar backlash for playing the role of Starr Carter in The Hate U Give, responded to the criticism in a since-deleted TikTok video posted on February 2025, noting that being “at odds with my own community,” felt more painful than the racism she received from being cast in the Star Wars universe.

The actor also acknowledged how colorism plays out in the industry and said that she only felt comfortable going after the role after meeting with Adeyemi and getting her blessing. 

“I had the opportunity to meet Tomi, the novelist, for the first time … And she goes, ‘Amandla, I want you to know that when you were a little girl and you were cast as Rue in The Hunger Games, and people said that Rue’s death wouldn’t be as sad because you’re a Black girl—that inspired me to write this series so that Black girls like you and Black girls of all shades could have a story written about them,’” Stenberg said. “We started crying, and I said to myself, ‘God wants me here.’”

During a June 2025 interview, podcaster Zethu Gqola asked Adeyemi about the criticism around the actor’s casting, to which the author responded that she “understand[s] when people are frustrated.” She also addressed the concerns over Nigerian representation.

“If you need me to be a punching bag, I get it because just like you, I’ve been hurt so many times by this industry and the feeling of being erased by it.” She added, “If you feel brokenhearted by this, I don’t think you’ll feel like that when you’re sitting in the theaters. I promise you, this world is so beautiful and we’re all in it and that’s so beautiful to me.”

During the interview, Adeyemi also noted that the film features Nigerian actors selected from the casting call filmmakers held across the West African country. 

The film also features Saniyya Sidney, Diaana Babnicova, Bukky Bakray, Ayra Starr, Pamilerin Afolake Ayodeji, Shamz Garuba, Kola Bodunde and Tèmítópé Fágbénlé.

July 4, 2026: Adeyemi begins distancing herself from the film

The author posted a cryptic TikTok video stating that she would not be watching the film. “There is a reason I will not post anything about the adaptation of my work. That’s all,” she wrote in a screenshotted conversation. The video has since been deleted. The post also included screenshots of a conversation between herself and Stenberg stemming from a text exchange in February 2025, around the time Stenberg posted their response to the casting criticism. 

“Do not ever use my name in an interview or video again. Do not text me. Do not call me,” the message read, according to the Los Angeles Times. Adeyemi also appeared to have blocked Stenberg.

Adeyemi was also noticeably absent from a special sneak peak screening at CinemaCon in April 2026.

July 27, 2026: The Children of Blood and Bone trailer drops

At a trailer premiere screening in Brooklyn on Monday, Prince-Bythewood said the film is “beautifully inspired by Nigeria and also inclusive of the whole diaspora. We wanted all of us to be able to see ourselves within this, just our complete and utter humanity, all the beautiful hues.”

July 29, 2026 Adeyemi recalls the day she left set hyperventilating

The day after Paramount released the film’s first trailer, Ayedemi shared a five-minute long TikTok discussing an undisclosed traumatic experience she had which prompted her to leave the “set of my own film adaptation, hyperventilating and sobbing.” Though she doesn’t go into much detail, she claims that she continued to be “antagonised” even after her departure. The author stated that if she didn’t ring the alarm, things would only get worse. 

She stated that she “suffered such severe somatic pain and so many panic attacks,” upon returning from Cape Town to America after filming. “I knew it was so bad that I would never ever be able to watch this film, and I made peace with that,” she said. 

What’s next?

We’re still six months away from this film’s release. Whether audiences find out what the controversy is centered on remains to be seen, especially considering the filmmakers and studio have yet to comment. It’s also too early to say whether or not Children of Virtue and Vengeance and Children of Anguish and Anarchy will also get screen adaptations.

Adeyemi was also set to make a cameo in the film. With her current stance on the film, it’s likely her appearance will not make the final cut. Her representatives told People that her current focus is promoting The Siren, her forthcoming novel which releases in September.

We’ll update this article with more details as the story unfolds…

title: How Influencer Toni Bravo became the CEO of Blush
text:
How Influencer Toni Bravo became the CEO of Blush

Toni Bravo is the CEO of Blush and an influencer powerhouse. Based in Los Angeles, the California native has built a loyal community well into the millions because of her impeccable taste and advocacy for inclusivity in the beauty industry. Toni joined host Brooke DeVard on the Naked Beauty Podcast to talk about her life before a viral blush try-on video changed everything. She shared what it was like to grow up as a fraternal twin in the sunny and very diverse Long Beach. They talk about her early forays into filming and editing herself and her family at just nine years old, simply for the love of storytelling. She detailed how influential the women in her life were to shaping the way she saw the beauty in herself and the world around her. It’s precisely this love of telling intimate stories that have shaped her POV into the one beloved by so many.

Toni doesn’t hold back when it comes to the realities of being a successful and full-time content creator, especially when advocating for dark-skinned Black women’s access to high-quality beauty. It was very interesting to learn how she maintains strong brand relationships without compromising the truth about product efficacy. She details the commitment and self-trust one has to have to succeed, because your point of view is everything. During their conversation, Toni talked about her interest in product development and why she isn’t limiting herself in anything. Toni also blessed the podcast with a quick tour of her favorite products, from skincare, to haircare, and of course blush! They covered her recent Architectural Digest feature and the intentional design choices that went into making her home, hers.

title: How Aora Beauty Founder Nour Tayara Made Sustainability Beautiful
text:
How Aora Beauty Founder Nour Tayara Made Sustainability Beautiful

Nour Tayara joins the Naked Beauty Podcast to talk about his innovative and 100% plastic-free beauty brand, AORA. During the conversation with host Brooke DeVard, he shared how he found his place in Lebanon’s underground queer scene and shaped his life’s motto to be kind and engaging to everyone, wherever you are. They talk about how Nour supplemented his scholarship by taking guerrilla marketing jobs and how they changed his mind about his electrical engineering major. Nour explains how an incredibly high test score landed him an internship and ultimately a full-time role at L’Oréal, where he worked for 13 years.

As Nour’s role and responsibilities evolved, he learned more about the waste and overconsumption plaguing the industry. Always prepared to innovate, he pitched a plastic-free brand to his management, which was promptly rejected. While reeling from a series of difficult events, Nour shared that a four-month break in Mexico City ultimately led him to his co-founder. The pair were aligned on building a brand that celebrates Mexican culture and is 100% plastic-free. Join them for an incredible conversation about what happens when you stay open to possibilities for your future and your principles are immovable. Nour details what it means to him to bring color to the clean beauty movement, why Mexico has always been a lifeline, and what it feels like to disrupt an industry.

title: Is Spider-Man: Brand New Day Worth Watching? Our Honest Review
text:
Is Spider-Man: Brand New Day Worth Watching? Our Honest Review

Zendaya and Tom Holland have been making waves with their Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour, but is the film worth watching? The anticipated sequel to Spider-Man: No Way Home has just hit theaters, and it’s a more grounded, serious look at Spider-Man’s life as he attempts to live life in solitude. The film has received an overwhelmingly positive response from critics, with a solid score of 91% on Rotten Tomatoes.

It’s easy to dismiss Spider-Man: No Way Home as a superhero film that’s all about action and big set pieces, but there’s a deep look into what makes you unique, how connection and relationships are so important, and it will make you want to call your best friend.

Below, entertainment writers Angeline Barion, Bernice Corral and Rachel Choy examine what makes Spider-Man: No Way Home so emotional, the acting performances from Sadie Sink, Zendaya and Tom Holland, and how many tissues they went through. Spoilers below.

Rachel Choy: How excited were you for this movie?!

Bernice Corral: Literally my most anticipated movie of the year. From Sony.

Angeline Barion: I’m not usually openly expressive about how much of a fan I am about things, except for minions. So this coming out around the same time meant I had an out of body experience. I think I almost blew up, like spontaneously combusted. That’s the level of excitement.

RC: I want to know the level of tissues. How many tissues did you use?

AB: I bought a packet of 60 Kleenex tissues, and I think that collectively between three of us sitting in the same row as really big Spider-Man fans, I think we got through 20, and we had like a whole plastic cup full.

RC: Let’s talk about the performances to begin with. What did you think of Tom Holland?

BC: I mean he’s great, but did he need to be topless that much?

RC: Yeah, he didn’t need to be in his undies. But also, he did. Wait, guys, can we talk about the moment he got his organic web?

AB: That was a bit red hot.

RC: It was like jizz. It was splurting, and I was like, did we need such a close up?

AB: But also, I was just thinking about the passage of how much time had passed from when he passed out to when he woke up in that web. He really put his body on the line in this particular movie, and I thought his performance was amazing.

RC: The yearning!

AB: You could see it in his eyes, and he was just stoic. He was just looking for MJ the whole time.

RC: But also low-key stalkerish because she doesn’t know who he is!

BC: Well, yeah. When he showed up to her apartment, I was like, that’s trespassing.

RC: I was like boy, just read her the letter! Don’t do this, please. And what did you think of newcomer Sadie Sink?

BC: I just love her. I watched her in Stranger Things, she’s great.

RC: She was so good as Jean Grey, and I love X-Men. I’m not the hugest Marvel girl. I dropped off a little bit, but I’ve watched all the old X-Men films and all the Spider-Man ones. The depth and emotion in her, with her backstory and how they were treated like animals, there’s a lot to unpack there. Very similar to how you’re treated in our world if you’re different.

AB: I’ve never watched any of her stuff before, so this is the first time I’ve ever encountered Sadie. I think I was so drawn to her because she has quite an expressive forehead and eyes. The top section of her face is quite expressive.

RC: Also, her power was so cool. You could physically see her jumping from person to person. It was such a big jerk.

AB: The extras were so good! They just took it full force, and the way they were moving around, I was like, this could actually happen in real life and you wouldn’t notice. So if any telepaths are out there, some of our brains are rot.

BC: You could tell when she was possessing them and how they were able to capture it. Yeah, wow, your IMDB is gonna be crazy after this.

RC: What did you think about Zendaya, our MJ?

BC: One of the wigs she was wearing wasn’t my fave.

AB: It was the second one.

BC: You’re wearing a wig.

RC: Wigs aside, the scene where she was possessed by Jean Grey and Peter Parker thought his MJ remembered him?! You knew it was coming. I was screaming.

BC: The switch she was able to do between MJ and then possessed by Jean.

AB: I’m floored by her. I have no words to describe or encapsulate how well she played that, and keeping it a secret as well. I think that was really hard, especially Tom being her actual husband. I think that that plays such a big part of it. But damn, that twist in the, I’m not gonna say it outright, but the twist in The Punisher’s house was devastating.

RC: It adds such a human quality to it because because there’s a lot of big scenes and set pieces, but I feel like the small scenes actually had the most impact.

BC: I feel like with her character MJ, it’s been very surface level for the past movies, but then this one we’re able to see her depth. People didn’t take her seriously as an actor until this year.

RC: She wasn’t in the first one very much, and they were so little and young, so now there’s all the years of trauma growing up. So there’s that scene in the Punisher’s house, but there was also the Lego scene.

BC: Don’t talk to me about that.

AB: No, no, no, no!

BC: It’s a movie about trauma.

AB: I love that they called back to her first performance though, with the drawing and Lego. I think that that was really special because it really ties their friendship together. Despite obviously having lost it and then coming back together, it’s the small things. You can go a length of time without talking to a person or seeing a person, but there’s always something that ties you together. And I think they really nailed how that chemistry works between the three of them in that Lego scene.

BC: It didn’t feel forced.

AB: They’re just hanging out. I feel like if they were just hanging out at someone’s house, that’s literally what they would do.

RC: The other big plot point is the inhibitor. How much of your DNA can you change before you become a completely different person?

AB: I thought that’s how they were going to write the Hulk out of the MCU, because he becomes a monster, and all that. But I think that’s such a side thought. This whole theme was great because it leans into the whole being yourself, showing your true colors to your friends, being open and honest and authentic, and how you don’t have to walk through things alone, even when they’re difficult. And even when Jean broke her inhibitor, and that’s how she was able to have the release. I think it really also feeds into that like plotline, that theme, that narrative.

RC: And it’s exhausting to try to be something that you’re not. Loneliness is such a big theme as well. He’s trying to do everything perfectly, but his body just says no.

BC: Reach out when you need to.

RC: Everyone needs connection, whether it’s relationships or friendships. It’s so important. The one critique I had was there were the cameos from the other MCU characters. Sometimes you just want more from the character that’s the title character. I know they need the crossover so it can set up the next Avengers. But I wanted more of Spider-Man.

AB: Him and Ned. I think that we, especially in this particular press tour, we’re so focused on like Tom’s and Zendaya. Their relationship is so beautiful and admirable, but I think that this film really leans on Peter and Ned as well, and their connection to each other. I wish we got to see more of that because, the guy in the chair is such an iconic part of the franchise for for Tom Holland’s Spider-Man. And with Ned’s aura blow up, he just had an extreme amount of confidence, but at the same time, he was still that little nerdy boy on the inside. I wish that we got to see more of him playing that part out.

RC: He’s such a genuine, friendly character. There’s nothing sinister, he’s just wholesome. I want more of that.

AB: Can they make side movies?

BC: Shorts, like Ned’s Side Quest!

RC: Where does it rank out of Tom Holland’s Spider-Man films?

BC: I will say No Way Home, I do love that… but I love Homecoming. This is genuinely really hard. I will say I love how they brought it back to street level with this one and it was grounded in reality. It wasn’t like a portal opens up.

RC: I think this is why I love this one the most.

BC: He’s just a little guy!

RC: I quite liked how depressed he was. Because then he’ll have to get happy. He’s at rock bottom, so he can only get better… we hope.

AB: Him being street level, that is so great.

BC: That is the core of what Spider-Man is.

AB: I don’t think it sensationalizes a multiverse and all of these infinite possibilities. I think it just focuses on the one possibility that sometimes things just don’t work out, and you have to find your way to to deal with it. Things that you thought were gonna be forever fall apart, but it just focuses on you doing the simple things, and I think that’s what is great about Spider-Man, and I think that’s what so many people love about Spider-Man.

RC: Is it worth watching?

AB: I think if you are a Spider-Man fan, I think you’ll be happy.

RC: If you’re a casual fan or a bit neutral?

AB: I think the good thing with Spider-Man is it can stand on its own. You don’t have to watch the other Marvel movies in order to understand it. I think that this one feels like it can create its own line. Obviously it connects to the MCU, but this can standalone. It lives within like the same universe as Homecoming and Far From Home.

I think it does it justice, and I think that everyone should watch it. Doesn’t matter if you’re a Spider-Man fan or you’re not a Spider-Man fan. Even if you’re just feeling like you’re going through something and you don’t have people around you, and that’s literally that’s that’s what it is. It makes me emotional because I was sitting next to my best friend, and we sometimes go periods of time where we don’t talk to each other.

RC: You have that connection.

AB: That drawing scene, she draws in the same style. So it was very emotional.

RC: I feel like that you have those friendships that you can go for years being apart. I’ve lived so many places and overseas for years. But my best friend since I was 14, every time I see her, it’s like nothing’s changed. And I feel like if I even if I forgot my memories and connected with her, I feel like she’s in my soul. You just know each other. You just get it.

AB: It’s part of your DNA.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is in theaters now.
